articles.title: Vigilance, not pause, answer to AI risks: IBM India & South Asia MD
articles.summary:
No form of technology should be "artificially paused" and the need is to stay vigilant and think ahead on how to work with AI, so that innovation isn't stifled while the right governance and usage are built around it, IBM India and South Asia Managing Director Sandip Patel said on Tuesday.
In an interview to PTI, Patel said IBM India has always been a critical part of global operations, not only because the company continues to participate in the growth market here, but also because it is a "hotbed of innovation".
Innovations from India can be scaled and applied anywhere in the world, he said, pointing to Indian innovations such as UPI.
Citing a specific IBM innovation, Patel said the company was "very privileged" to be a part of the creation of YONO, the digital platform run by SBI. He called it a fairly unique proposition that has emerged from India and can be applied around the world.
As AI scales, IBM expects to keep participating in the growth story with India as a strong base

articles.title: Fighting to restore democracy in India: Rahul
articles.summary: New Delhi: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged electoral irregularities had a singular objective of restoring democracy in the country.Addressing the gathering after a high tea meeting at his residence with INDIA bloc leaders, opposition MPs and student organisations, Gandhi accused the government of undermining democratic institutions and said the opposition would jointly fight to restore democratic rule."There is no parallel protest; there is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: the restoration of democracy in India. Democracy has been destroyed, the Election Commission is destroyed, the Constitution is torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule in this country," Gandhi said.He also said the opposition would challenge the government's decision to restrict the use of Jantar Mantar as a protest site for expressing democratic dissent.He said, "One method of democracy was Jantar Mantar, but now the government has decided that Jantar Mantar can no longer be used to express democratic feeling, and we are going to challenge that idea. It cannot be so simple for the government to decide that the Indian people will not fight for their voice."He alleged PM Narendra Modi as the main "architect", Home Minister Amit Shah as the "implementer" of destroying the Indian Constitution."The people who have done this: Modi, the main architect; Amit Shah, the implementer; and Gyanesh Kumar. They need to understand that the net is closing around them. It is not going to be so simple that you can destroy the Indian Constitution and get away with it," Gandhi said.After the meeting, Kerala Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the INDIA bloc and the Congress would continue their fight against the Election Commission, alleging that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had damaged the electoral process."We will continue with the fight because Gyanesh Kumar has completely ruined the election process. INDIA alliance and the Congress party will fight to the last. One thing is very clear: everybody is united, and we will fight against the misdeeds of the Central Government and especially Gyanesh Kumar," Chennithala said.He also alleged that a file concerning Kumar's alleged misconduct and corruption during his tenure as Public Works Department (PWD) secretary in Kerala around 20 years ago was being examined by the state government."I received an application regarding the misconduct and corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar 20 years back when he was a PWD secretary in Kerala. We are going into the details of the file. In the file, it is very clear that he is involved in various corrupt activities," he alleged."Now, the Kerala government has decided to unearth all these things, and in the coming days, after going into the details, we will take a strong view on these corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar. It is already with the Director and the Anti-Corruption Bureau of Kerala," Chennithala added.

articles.title: NASA's Perseverance sets Mars record
articles.summary: WASHINGTON: NASA's robotic Perseverance rover has now driven farther than any other vehicle on the surface of any world other than Earth, racking up 28.1 miles (45.2 km) since arriving on Mars in 2021, the US space agency said on Tuesday.The car-sized, six-wheeled rover reached the milestone 5-1/2 years into its mission to explore if conditions conducive to microbial life ever existed on Earth's neighbor.In doing so, it is visiting some of the most ancient terrain ever encountered in the solar system."Perseverance's engineering hardware and instruments are in excellent shape with all redundant systems still available," Steven Lee of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, told Reuters."A recent assessment of all systems concluded that they are capable of operating well into the 2030s, likely beyond," added Lee, the project manager for NASA's two Mars rovers, Perseverance and Curiosity.Perseverance has exceeded the previous figure of 28.06 miles (45 km) driven on the Martian surface by NASA's Opportunity rover from 2004 to 2018. Both also exceeded the driving distances of any lunar rover.TRAVERSING JEZERO CRATERPerseverance, with its suite of scientific instruments, has focused on the Jezero Crater, a region in the northern hemisphere of Mars believed to have been flooded with water and home to a lake basin billions of years ago.The rover set the milestone in a journey toward an area called Idubi, through the region off the crater's western rim nicknamed Lac de Charmes.Its companion rover, Curiosity, rolls along in the Gale Crater near the Martian equator.Perseverance is showing no signs of slowing down, Lee added.Its mobility system mechanisms are being tested to show it can drive 100 km (62 miles) or more, he said, with the hardware to be tested to the equivalent of 150 km to 300 km (93 miles to 186 miles) in the effort.NASA attributed a major role in Perseverance's success to its self-driving capability, an autonomous navigation system called AutoNav. Lee said 90% of its drives are done autonomously, with no human intervention."Perseverance takes stereo images of the terrain ahead, generates a 3D software map, and selects the safest path towards a drive goal," he said.Another key component is the Vision Compute Element, a fast co-processor computer that allows the rover to process images and run its self-driving software very quickly, almost continuously during drives, Lee added.That contrasts with previous rovers, which needed to pause to "think" before each drive segment, he said."Perseverance builds on the 29-year legacy of our past Mars rovers - Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity - each incorporating prior lessons and improving our ability to drive on another world," Lee said.POTENTIAL BIOSIGNATURELee said the rover's biggest achievement was almost certainly its discovery, unveiled last year, of a potential biosignature, or possible sign of ancient microbial life.This was found in reddish rock believed to have formed 3.2 billion to 3.8 billion years ago in a river channel feeding the lake that once filled Jezero Crater.The Lac de Charmes terrain, Lee said, may yield clues to early planetary geological processes, such as the effects of large meteorite impacts. Jezero Crater was formed by such an impact early in Martian history.Lee cited orbital evidence that some areas of the rim were once hydrothermal systems with warm or hot groundwater."These areas may once have provided a warm, watery subsurface environment conducive to life," he added. "Indeed, some paleontologists hypothesize that life on Earth began in such environments."The rover's original mission envisaged just 12.4 miles (20 km) of driving. NASA recently approved an extension of its mission to explore the crater rim until roughly the end of 2028.The rover's plutonium-based power system is performing as expected, Lee said, adding it has "many years of useful energy still available."

articles.title: IMF raises India’s 2026 growth aim to 7%
articles.summary: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday, raised India’s growth forecast for 2026 to 7% from 6.4% projected in July, citing stronger-than-expected momentum, resilient domestic demand and robust services activity despite higher oil prices.The IMF’s latest assessment also sets India apart from several energy-importing emerging economies facing a weaker medium-term outlook.Also Read: IMF edges up 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% but warns economy is ‘vulnerable to setbacks from both directions’“India stands out with upward revisions,” the IMF said in its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, pointing to growing evidence of stronger growth potential.The IMF projected global output to expand at an average annual pace of 3.2% in 2028–31, below the pre-pandemic average of 3.7% recorded during 2000–19.It said medium-term downgrades were concentrated among economies directly affected by the Middle East conflict and energy-importing emerging and developing economies, with India an exception.134908208Domestic demand drives latest upgradeThe Fund raised its India growth forecast for 2026 by 0.6 percentage points from its July outlook and 0.5 percentage points from April. Its projection for 2027 was also revised upwards to 7%, up 0.3 percentage points from July and 0.5 percentage points from April.These upgrades add to a growing consensus among global forecasters that India’s economy is proving more resilient than expected, following stronger-than-anticipated growth in the first quarter. The World Bank and the OECD have also raised their forecasts, while other major agencies expect the economy to expand at around 7%.The Fund attributed the stronger outlook to resilient domestic demand and robust services activity, which have helped cushion the economy against higher global oil prices.“The region (Asia) has been incredibly resilient, even though its economies are net importers of energy and other commodities. The AI boom has more than offset the headwinds from commodity markets, with China and India emerging as the big engines of growth,” said Silvana Tenreyro, IMF economic counsellor and director of the Research Department.Tenreyro said the Fund had revised its growth forecasts for both China and India upwards, with India receiving a sizeable upgrade.China’s growth is projected to ease to 4.5% in 2026 and 4% in 2027, as higher oil prices, prolonged uncertainty and structural headwinds weigh on economic activity.India bucks weaker medium-term trendThe Fund linked India’s improved outlook to sustained economic momentum and stronger growth potential, supported by favourable demographic dynamics, a growing domestic market and structural reforms.Also Read: After S&P & Fitch, ADB raises India's growth aim to 7% but El Nino clouds food storyHowever, the brighter projections do not remove the risks facing the economy. Higher oil prices remain a vulnerability for India, while persistent global uncertainty could weigh on demand and growth.

articles.summary: New Delhi: The Harvard Club of India has clarified that it has neither issued nor endorsed any statement concerning the recent protests in New Delhi and the actions taken by authorities in connection with the agitation against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Rajat Sethi, an Executive Committee member of the Harvard Club of India, clarified the organisation's position while speaking to ANI."As a member of the elected body of the Executive Council of the Harvard Club of India, which is the official alumni group of Harvard University alumni in India, I wanted to issue a clarification that certain individuals have gone ahead and issued a letter remarking on and making comments about the recent protest and the detention that followed. I wanted to issue a clarification that this is not the official position of the Harvard Club of India," Sethi said.He further said that the Club's charter and mandate prohibit it from issuing political statements on its own behalf or on behalf of Harvard University."Therefore, this clarification is to explain to the larger audience that certain individuals who happen to be alumni of Harvard University have issued the statement in their personal capacity. While we respect personal expression, that is not a substitute for institutional representation," he added.In an official statement, the Club said that a statement reportedly issued by a group of individuals identifying themselves as Harvard University alumni, commenting on police action against protesters and the detention of certain individuals, reflected only the personal views of its signatories.It stated, "This is to clarify that the Harvard Club of India, the officially recognised alumni association representing Harvard University alumni in India, has neither issued nor endorsed any statement concerning the recent protests in New Delhi or the actions taken by the authorities in connection with these events. A statement reportedly issued by a group of individuals identifying themselves as Harvard University alumni, expressing views on the police action against protesters and the detention of certain individuals, represents the personal views of its signatories alone."The Club said the statement should not be construed as its official position or as an institutional endorsement."It should not be construed as reflecting the official position, views, or institutional endorsement of the Harvard Club of India, the statement read.The Harvard Club of India said its governing bylaws do not authorise individuals or groups to make political statements or express positions on behalf of the Club or Harvard University.The Club reiterated its commitment to maintaining a clear distinction between individual expression and official institutional representation.

articles.title: Investors shrug off bear party, put big money into equity mutual funds
articles.summary: Mumbai: Equity mutual fund inflows hit a five-month high in September, with investors pouring money into small- and mid-cap schemes despite a weak equity market backdrop and sustained foreign investor selling. Debt funds, however, witnessed outflows, led by redemptions from liquid and money market schemes by companies for advance tax payments, partly resulting in the mutual fund industry posting outflows during the month.Net inflows into equity schemes rose nearly 31% from the prior month to ₹38,306.55 crore in September, extending the momentum seen in August when investments increased nearly 19%, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India. With September's inflows, equity funds have now recorded net inflows for 67 consecutive months.Contributions under monthly systematic investment plans (SIPs) hit a monthly record at ₹32,490 crore in September, up from ₹32,297 crore in August. SIP assets under management rose to ₹17.86 lakh crore.134905091The strong inflows came even as both the Sensex and Nifty indexes declined about 6% during the month on concerns over rising crude oil prices, higher US bond yields and continued selling by foreign portfolio investors.Among equity categories, small-cap funds attracted the highest inflows at ₹9,038.57 crore, followed by mid-cap at ₹7,834.84 crore. Together, the two segments accounted for about 44% of the total inflows into equity funds. Investors continue to favour mid- and small-cap categories despite their relatively weak recent performance, said Viraj Gandhi, CEO of Samco Mutual Fund."The 12-month benchmark performance was mixed as the large-cap index fell 12% and the mid-cap index fell 1%, while the small-cap index rose 3%. Against that backdrop, September's equity-fund flows suggest investors were still favouring mid- and small-cap exposure despite their recent weak performance," Gandhi said.Flexi-cap funds received ₹6,701.80 crore during the month, up from ₹5,059.42 crore in August, while large-cap funds returned to the positive territory with net inflows of ₹859.47 crore after witnessing net outflows of ₹1,147 crore in the previous month.Read more: Jubilant Pharmova block deal: Quant Mutual Fund offloads Rs 190 crore stake amid Rs 800 crore fundraising plan; Abakkus buys 11 lakh sharesHowever, the number of systematic investment plans accounts presented a contrasting picture. Around 6.3 million new SIP accounts were registered last month, while nearly 7.3 million matured or were discontinued, resulting in closures and maturities exceeding fresh registrations by about a million.Debt FundsDebt funds witnessed a sharp reversal, with net outflows surging to ₹1.83 lakh crore in September from ₹8,127.32 crore in August. Liquid funds accounted for the bulk of the withdrawals, recording net outflows of ₹95,743.20 crore compared with inflows of ₹19,934.29 crore in August. Money market funds also saw net outflows of ₹50,846.21 crore after attracting ₹11,734.71 crore in the previous month.The sharp pullback from debt funds dragged the industry's overall flows into the negative territory. The mutual fund industry reported net outflows of ₹1.33 lakh crore in September compared with net inflows of ₹41,368.05 crore in August.Read more: HCL Tech Q2 Results: Profit jumps 21% YoY to Rs 5,132 crore; co declares Rs 12/share dividend"The decline was overwhelmingly driven by liquidity-oriented categories, suggesting quarter-end treasury adjustments and institutional cash-management activity rather than a broad-based deterioration in investor appetite for fixed income," said Nehal Meshram, senior analyst at Morningstar Investment Research India.The industry's total assets under management declined 5.1% to ₹82.64 lakh crore as of September 30 from ₹87.08 lakh crore in August, largely reflecting the sharp outflows from debt-oriented schemes and mark-to-market impact from the fall in equities.Gold ETFs saw monthly inflows of ₹4,451 crore, marking a 71% jump from ₹2,597 crore in August, as investors turned to the safe-haven asset amid geopolitical tensions.
